content.text:
Nature and science facts about Tyrannosaurus

T. rex lived in North America in the late Cretaceous, about 66 million years ago. It was a giant, roughly 12 m long and weighing 6–9 tons. Its around 60 teeth were up to 20 cm long, and its bite force was tremendous. Its front arms, with two fingers, were small but strong, and with forward-facing eyes it judged distances well. Today's birds are the descendants of dinosaurs.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How big was Tyrannosaurus?
A. It was a huge dinosaur about 12 m long and weighing 6–9 tons. Its teeth were about 20 cm long.

Q. Why are its front arms so small?
A. They were small but muscularly strong. Because it hunted with its big head and jaws, small front arms were enough.

Q. How can we enjoy this at home?
A. Sense its size by measuring heights, look at dinosaur models and guides, and talk about how "birds are the descendants of dinosaurs."
